data_schema.title: USDA Directive Extraction Schema v2.1 (DR/DM)
data_schema.description: Extracts metadata and structured policy statements from 3000 series USDA Departmental Regulation (DR) or Departmental Manual (DM). Governing rules: (1) Any field described as verbatim must be copied character-for-character from the source document. Never paraphrase, merge, abbreviate, summarize, or insert ellipses. (2) Do not infer. If the source does not support an optional field, leave the field out entirely. Never return an empty string or a guess. (3) Only the label fields in policy_statements (statement_kind, statement_function, modal_use, normative_force, actor_basis) are interpretations. Every other field is quoted or copied from the document.

document_type.description: Type of document as printed in the header, such as 'Departmental Regulation' or 'Departmental Manual'.

issuing_organization.description: Organization issuing the document, verbatim from the header.

issuing_location.description: Location of the issuing organization, verbatim from the header.

regulation_number.description: Official document number from the header, verbatim, for example 'DR 3105-001'.

subject.description: Subject or title of the document, verbatim from the header.

issue_date.description: Issue date from the header, as written.

expiration_date.description: Expiration date from the header, as written. Leave out if none is printed.

opi.description: Office of Primary Interest (OPI) from the header, verbatim.

supersedes.description: The prior document this document supersedes. Take all values from the supersession paragraph in the body (usually under Special Instructions/Cancellations), NOT from the header. Leave the whole object out if the document supersedes nothing.

document_number.description: Number of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph. If it is identical to this document's own number, still copy it from the supersession paragraph, not the header.

document_title.description: Title of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

document_date.description: Date of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

scope.description: The text of the Scope section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Scope section.

purpose.description: The text of the Purpose section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Purpose section.

inquiries.description: Contact information from the Inquiries section. Leave out any property the document does not state; never return an empty string.

office.description: Office or division named for inquiries, verbatim. Leave out if the document names no office.

email.description: Email address given for inquiries, verbatim, without trailing punctuation. Leave out if none is given.

table_of_contents.description: Top-level entries of the printed table of contents, in order, including appendices. Return an empty list if the document prints no table of contents.

section_number.description: Section or appendix identifier as printed, for example '1.' or 'Appendix A'.

section_title.description: Section or appendix title as printed in the table of contents.

page.description: Page number exactly as printed in the table of contents, for example '2' or 'A-1'. Copy it even if the section actually starts on a different page. Leave out if no page number is printed.

actors.description: Registry of every distinct entity that the policy text names in an acting role. One entry per entity. Include every entity used as actor_name in policy_statements. Also include entities the document names in a role without being directed to act (mark those mentioned_only). Documents (bylaws, regulations, directives) are NEVER actors and must not appear here. Return an empty list if the document names no actors.

name.description: The entity's name exactly as written in the policy text, without a leading article ('the') and without a possessive. Keep a compound name intact if the document writes it as one phrase, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'. This is the join key used by actor_name in policy_statements, so spell it identically there.

components.description: ONLY for a name that joins separate entities with commas or 'and' (for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices' gives 'USDA Mission Areas', 'agencies', 'staff offices'). NEVER split a job title from the organization that qualifies it ('Director of IT, Office of the Inspector General' is ONE position), and never split an organization name from the position it modifies ('Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Associate CIOs (ACIO)' is ONE group). Each component is a verbatim substring of the name. Leave out for single entities.

items.description: One verbatim component of a compound actor name.

actor_type.description: Kind of entity. Use exactly one of: position (a job title, singular or plural, for example 'USDA CIO' or 'Mission Area Assistant CIOs'), office (an organizational unit, for example 'OCIO Executive Secretariat'), council_or_body (a council, committee, board, or similar body), group (a category of organizations or units, not job titles, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'), external_entity (an entity outside the document's authority), program_or_system (an IT initiative, system, program, or project that the document says must act or conform).

binding_status.description: bound_by_this_document: the document directs, permits, or assigns a function or role to this entity and has authority over it. mentioned_only: the document names the entity but cannot or does not impose anything on it (for example a council or agency outside USDA that the document says a USDA body partners with).

policy_statements.description: Structured statements from the numbered body sections only (not the table of contents, not the appendices). RULES. (a) SENTENCES: emit one statement per sentence. If a paragraph has more than one sentence, give each its own statement with ids suffixed .s1, .s2, and so on. Abbreviations and legal citations ('U.S.C.', 'CFR', '§', 'et seq.') do not end a sentence. (b) LISTS: when text introduces a list (usually ends with a colon, for example 'The USDA CIO will:'), emit the introducing text as one statement with statement_kind 'lead_in', and emit EVERY item of the list as its own statement with statement_kind 'list_item' and parent_statement_id set to the id of the lead_in. Never skip list items, including lists of legal authorities. For a list inside a list, parent_statement_id is the immediate parent. (c) NEVER merge text from different sentences, paragraphs, or list items into one statement. (d) Copy text exactly; do not summarize. (e) PRONOUNS: when a sentence's subject is a pronoun ('It', 'Its', 'They') that refers to a named actor in the preceding sentence, resolve it: set actor_name to that actor and actor_basis to resolved_from_prior_sentence. (f) DOCUMENT AS SUBJECT: when the grammatical subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'), leave actor_name out; the entities the document acts on belong in target.

statement_id.description: Printed numbering path of the statement: section number, then paragraph letter, then item number in parentheses, for example '1', '3.a', '5.d.s2', '6.a(1)'. Add '.sN' only when a paragraph contains more than one sentence. Must be unique within the document.

statement_kind.description: standalone: a complete sentence that stands on its own. lead_in: text that introduces a list and is incomplete without its items. list_item: a list item that completes its lead_in.

parent_statement_id.description: Include ONLY when statement_kind is list_item: the statement_id of its immediate lead_in. For every other statement leave this field out entirely; never return an empty string.

section_number.description: Number of the section containing the statement, digits only, for example '6'.

section_title.description: Title of the section containing the statement, as shown in the table of contents, for example 'Roles and Responsibilities'.

source_text.description: VERBATIM text of this one sentence or list item exactly as printed, including trailing punctuation such as ':' or ';' and including any list-ending words such as 'and'. No paraphrase, no ellipses, no text from any other statement. For a list_item, give only the item's own text, not the lead_in.

statement_function.description: What the statement does. obligation: a required action or compliance requirement on an actor. responsibility: a standing duty or function assigned to an actor, including present-tense descriptions of what a body does. role_designation: assigns an entity to a role, for example membership or voting status. authority: names a legal source of authority or a grant of authority. scope: states what or whom the document applies to. purpose: states why the document or a body exists. definition: defines a term. condition: states a standalone triggering condition. exception: carves out an exception. savings_clause: states that the document does not displace existing authorities or delegations. effectivity: states when the document takes effect or how long it lasts. supersession: states that the document replaces another. classification_rule: states a rule that classifies something or applies a requirement when a status is met. reference: points to another document or location. inquiry: tells who may be contacted. container: use for every lead_in statement. other: none of the above.

modal_verb.description: The modal word or phrase of the statement's MAIN clause, exactly as written, for example 'will', 'can', 'may', 'must', 'shall', 'must not'. Ignore modals inside relative or subordinate clauses (for 'advises the USDA CIO on IT matters that may become IT investments', the 'may' is not the statement's modal). For a list_item whose own text has no modal, copy the modal from its lead_in. Leave out if the main clause has no modal.

modal_use.description: deontic: the main-clause modal directs, permits, or prohibits action by an actor (for example 'The Deputy CIO will serve', 'can direct questions'). predictive: the modal only states what will happen or remain true (for example 'It will remain in effect until superseded'). none: the main clause has no modal.

normative_force.description: mandatory: deontic 'will', 'shall', or 'must' directing an actor to act or to serve in a role. prohibitive: deontic 'must not', 'shall not', or 'may not'. permissive: deontic 'may' or 'can'. assigned: a present-tense statement with no deontic modal that assigns or describes a function, duty, or role of a named actor (for example 'The CIO Council advises the USDA CIO on...', 'It assesses the needs of...'); use it only when actor_name is present, and never for purpose statements. descriptive: everything else with no deontic force, including purpose, scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, references, authorities, definitions, and statements about the document itself or about other documents. not_applicable: use for every lead_in; its force is carried by its list_items.

actor_name.description: The entity directed to act, permitted to act, or assigned a function or role by this statement, spelled exactly as in the matching actors[].name. It must appear in source_text or in the lead_in's text (leading article removed); for a resolved pronoun, copy it from the antecedent sentence. Leave out when the statement binds no actor: scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, statements about documents (including bylaws), and any statement whose subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'). Never supply an actor that is not stated in the text or resolvable from the preceding sentence. Always leave out for lead_in statements.

actor_basis.description: Include ONLY when actor_name is present; otherwise leave this field out entirely. explicit_in_statement: the actor appears in this statement's own source_text. inherited_from_lead_in: the actor appears only in the lead_in that this list_item completes. resolved_from_prior_sentence: the subject is a pronoun resolved to the actor named in the preceding sentence.

target.description: VERBATIM phrase naming what the action is directed at or what the statement applies to, starting at the first word after any leading article ('a', 'an', 'the'). For a role_designation, the body or unit the role is within (for example 'CIO Council'). Leave out if none.

resulting_status.description: VERBATIM phrase naming the status or role that a role_designation or classification_rule confers, for example 'voting member' or 'advisory (non-voting) members'. Leave out for other statements.

conditions.description: VERBATIM phrases that restrict when or to what the statement applies, for example 'that the CIO Council designates as enterprise initiatives'. Do NOT treat a non-restrictive descriptive phrase set off by commas (for example 'appointed by the USDA CIO' in 'The Secretariat, appointed by the USDA CIO, will serve') as a condition. Leave out if there are none.

items.description: One verbatim condition phrase copied from source_text.

cross_references.description: Other documents, laws, or regulations cited in source_text, each copied verbatim as ONE entry per cited authority, including its code citation (for example 'The Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 11101 et seq.' is one entry; for a list_item that is just a citation, the entry is the item text without the trailing ';' or 'and'). Never add a separate entry for a title that is part of the same citation (the words 'Chief Information Officer' after '7 CFR § 2.32'). Never list generic categories such as 'law' or 'Federal regulation'. Leave out if none.

acronyms.description: Acronyms and abbreviations listed in the acronym appendix, one entry per row, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no acronym appendix.

acronym.description: Acronym or abbreviation exactly as printed.

authorities_and_references.description: Entries of the Authorities and References appendix, one per entry, each copied verbatim, including any date, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no such appendix.

items.description: One appendix entry exactly as printed, joined across line breaks.

extract_result.subject: USDA Classified National Security Information Program
extract_result.opi: Office of Homeland Security and Emergency Coordination
extract_result.purpose: This regulation prescribes Departmental roles and responsibilities for the classification, declassification, and safeguarding of classified national security information, and promulgates a revised Departmental Manual (DM) 3440-001, USDA Information Security Program Manual.

actors.name: all employees holding national security clearances
Office of Homeland Security and Emergency Coordination (OHSEC), Personnel and Document Security Division (PDSD)
components: Office of Homeland Security and Emergency Coordination (OHSEC)

actors.name: Subcabinet Officers, Agency Administrators, and Office Directors
Employees, contractors, and individuals maintaining a security clearance for working with classified information at USDA
components: individuals maintaining a security clearance for working with classified information at USDA

policy_statements.source_text: This regulation prescribes Departmental roles and responsibilities for the classification, declassification, and safeguarding of classified national security information, and promulgates a revised Departmental Manual (DM) 3440-001, USDA Information Security Program Manual.
This regulation supersedes Departmental Regulation (DR) 3440-001, dated October 5, 2011.

The Secretary of Agriculture has been delegated the Original Classification Authority (OCA) by Presidential Order (75 Federal Register [FR] 735), effective December 29, 2009, and may classify USDA information as either Confidential or Secret.

Executive Order (E.O.) 13526 “Classified National Security Information” (hereafter, E.O. 13526) and 32 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Part 2001 “Classified National Security Information Implementing Directive No.1” (hereafter 32 CFR Part 2001) establish the minimum standards and procedures for protecting classified national security information (hereafter, classified information).
cross_references: Executive Order (E.O.) 13526 “Classified National Security Information” (hereafter, E.O. 13526)
32 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Part 2001 “Classified National Security Information Implementing Directive No.1” (hereafter 32 CFR Part 2001)

policy_statements.source_text: Security procedures and guidance are detailed in DM 3440-001 “Classified National Security Information Program Manual.”
cross_references: DM 3440-001 “Classified National Security Information Program Manual”

policy_statements.source_text: Departmental Agencies and Offices must comply with E.O. 13526, 32 CFR Part 2001, and this DR.
policy_statements.target: E.O. 13526, 32 CFR Part 2001, and this DR

policy_statements.source_text: This DR is applicable to USDA employees, contractors and individuals who serve in advisory, consultant, or non-employee affiliate capacities who have been granted access to classified information.
conditions: who have been granted access to classified information

policy_statements.source_text: It is the Policy of USDA that:
The Secretary may base a classification determination on one (1) or more of the following categories:
Military plans, weapons systems, or operations;
Foreign government information;
Intelligence activities (including covert action), intelligence sources or methods or cryptology;
Foreign relations or foreign activities of the United States, including confidential sources;
Scientific, technological, or economic matters relating to the national security;
Vulnerabilities or capabilities of systems, installations, infrastructures, projects, plans or protection services relating to the national security; and
The development, production or use of weapons of mass destruction.
Information may be originally classified under the terms of E.O. 13526, only if all the following conditions are met:
An original classification authority is classifying the information;
The information is owned by, produced by or for, or is under the control of the United States Government;
The information falls within one (1) or more of the categories of information listed above in paragraph 4 (a); and

The original classification authority determines that the unauthorized disclosure of the information reasonably could be expected to result in damage to the national security, which includes defense against transnational terrorism, and the original classification authority is able to identify or describe the damage.
policy_statements.target: the unauthorized disclosure of the information

policy_statements.source_text: Classified national security information consists of information that has been determined pursuant to E.O. 13526 to require protection against unauthorized disclosure and is marked to indicate its classified status when in documentary form in accordance with E.O. 13526 and DM 3440-001.
Minimum safeguarding of classified information requires storage in a General Services Administration (GSA) approved security container.
Security containers meeting the standards and specifications established by GSA may be procured through the Federal Supply System.
conditions: meeting the standards and specifications established by GSA

policy_statements.source_text: If there is any significant doubt about the need to classify information, it shall not be classified.
conditions: If there is any significant doubt about the need to classify information

policy_statements.source_text: This provision does not:
Amplify or modify the substantive criteria or procedures for classification; or
policy_statements.target: the substantive criteria or procedures for classification

policy_statements.source_text: Create any substantive or procedural rights subject to judicial review.
policy_statements.target: any substantive or procedural rights subject to judicial review

policy_statements.source_text: USDA Agencies shall prevent unnecessary access to classified information by establishing a need for access to classified information, limiting access to a minimum consistent with operational and security requirements and needs, and ensuring classified information is not released to, or shared with, persons who do not possess an active security clearance equal to or higher than the classification level of the material in question.

Whenever practicable, use a classified addendum whenever classified information constitutes a small portion of an otherwise unclassified document or prepare a product to allow for dissemination at the lowest level of classification possible or unclassified form.
conditions: whenever classified information constitutes a small portion of an otherwise unclassified document

policy_statements.source_text: USDA will ensure declassification of information as soon as feasible, but not longer than 25 years from the time of classification.
Declassification is accomplished using the systematic, automatic, and mandatory declassification processes outlined in E.O. 13526.
Continuous security awareness training is required of all employees holding national security clearances.
policy_statements.actor_name: all employees holding national security clearances

policy_statements.source_text: Training will be coordinated and presented by the Office of Homeland Security and Emergency Coordination (OHSEC), Personnel and Document Security Division (PDSD).
policy_statements.actor_name: Office of Homeland Security and Emergency Coordination (OHSEC), Personnel and Document Security Division (PDSD)

policy_statements.source_text: Destruction and disposal of classified information must be done in compliance with E.O. 13526 and 32 CFR Part 2001.
policy_statements.target: Destruction and disposal of classified information

policy_statements.source_text: Confidential and Secret information can be shredded using a National Security Agency (NSA) approved shredder.
NSA approved shredders may be procured through the Federal Supply System.

Incidents involving the mishandling of classified information must be reported to the Agency’s Information Security Coordinator and the PDSD Classified National Security Program Branch immediately upon discovery.
policy_statements.target: the Agency’s Information Security Coordinator and the PDSD Classified National Security Program Branch
conditions: involving the mishandling of classified information

policy_statements.source_text: The Secretary of Agriculture is delegated as the OCA for USDA.
The Secretary must designate a Senior Agency Official (SAO) responsible for the development and administration of the Classified National Security Information Program (CNSIP).
conditions: responsible for the development and administration of the Classified National Security Information Program (CNSIP)

policy_statements.source_text: This designation is currently in a delegation of authority made to the Assistant Secretary for Departmental Management and has been re-delegated to the Director of OHSEC.
The Senior Agency Official is required to maintain a Top Secret clearance.
The Senior Agency Official is the primary liaison between USDA and the Information Security Oversight Office (ISOO).
policy_statements.target: USDA and the Information Security Oversight Office (ISOO)

policy_statements.source_text: This position is responsible for identifying necessary resources to manage the CNSIP and providing program oversight.
policy_statements.target: necessary resources to manage the CNSIP and providing program oversight

policy_statements.source_text: Subcabinet Officers, Agency Administrators, and Office Directors, whose organizations require access to classified material are responsible for:
conditions: whose organizations require access to classified material

policy_statements.source_text: Designating an Information Security Coordinator to serve as a liaison to PDSD;
policy_statements.actor_name: Subcabinet Officers, Agency Administrators, and Office Directors

policy_statements.source_text: Providing subject matter experts to assist with the development of recommendations for the Secretary to exercise the OCA;
policy_statements.actor_name: Subcabinet Officers, Agency Administrators, and Office Directors

policy_statements.source_text: Ensuring classified information is created, marked, stored, transmitted, and destroyed in accordance with this DR and DM 3440-001;
policy_statements.actor_name: Subcabinet Officers, Agency Administrators, and Office Directors

policy_statements.source_text: Ensuring the number of persons granted access to classified information is limited to those with a “need-to-know” to effectively carry out USDA program responsibilities;
policy_statements.actor_name: Subcabinet Officers, Agency Administrators, and Office Directors
policy_statements.target: the number of persons granted access to classified information

policy_statements.source_text: Ensuring employees who hold a security clearance receive initial security indoctrination training, annual security refresher training, derivative classification training, and a debriefing after classified information access is no longer required;
policy_statements.actor_name: Subcabinet Officers, Agency Administrators, and Office Directors
policy_statements.target: employees who hold a security clearance

policy_statements.source_text: Providing PDSD an annual updated list of individual within their Agency who is authorized to apply derivative classification marking;
policy_statements.actor_name: Subcabinet Officers, Agency Administrators, and Office Directors

policy_statements.source_text: Ensuring their organization conduct, complete and report the finding of the self-inspection to PDSD no later than the second week of August annually; and
policy_statements.actor_name: Subcabinet Officers, Agency Administrators, and Office Directors

policy_statements.source_text: Ensuring the performance standards includes the designation and management of classified information as a critical element, or an item to be evaluated in the rating of:
Original classification authority;
policy_statements.actor_name: Subcabinet Officers, Agency Administrators, and Office Directors

policy_statements.source_text: Security managers or security specialist; and
policy_statements.actor_name: Subcabinet Officers, Agency Administrators, and Office Directors

policy_statements.source_text: Of all personnel who duties significantly involve the creation or handling of classified information and personnel who regularly apply derivative classification markings.
policy_statements.actor_name: Subcabinet Officers, Agency Administrators, and Office Directors

policy_statements.source_text: The Director of OHSEC is responsible for:
Establishing and administering the USDA CNSIP in accordance with E.O. 13526, 32 CFR Part 2001, and this DR;
Maintaining an oversight role to ensure consistent and effective implementation of the Information Security Program throughout USDA;
Serving as the Deciding Official for the suspension, denial, and revocation of security clearances involving USDA personnel;
policy_statements.target: the suspension, denial, and revocation of security clearances involving USDA personnel

policy_statements.source_text: Granting a waiver for individuals who fail to complete required training for original classification and derivative classification authority due to unavoidable circumstances;
policy_statements.target: a waiver for individuals who fail to complete required training for original classification and derivative classification authority

policy_statements.source_text: Suspending classification authority of those individuals who fail to complete mandatory training for original classification to include declassification or derivative classification and has not been granted a waiver;
policy_statements.target: classification authority of those individuals who fail to complete mandatory training for original classification to include declassification or derivative classification and has not been granted a waiver

policy_statements.source_text: Ensuring USDA Classification Guide is reviewed at a minimum of once every five (5) years, or upon regulatory changes;
conditions: at a minimum of once every five (5) years, or upon regulatory changes

policy_statements.source_text: Establishing a system for processing, tracking and recording formal classification challenges made by authorized holders;
policy_statements.target: a system for processing, tracking and recording formal classification challenges made by authorized holders

policy_statements.source_text: Advising authorized holders of their rights to appeal to the Interagency Security Classification Appeals Panel (ISCAP) the decisions of the Agency on their challenge;
Ensuring PDSD reports the annual completion of self-inspections report by Agencies that receive, generate, process and store classified information;
Verifying the accuracy of information provided on the self-inspections reports prior to submitting report to ISOO;
policy_statements.target: the accuracy of information provided on the self-inspections reports
conditions: prior to submitting report to ISOO

policy_statements.source_text: Coordinating with the SAO the submission of the annual report to ISOO; and
Reporting security violations and/or improper declassifications to the Director of ISOO.
The Chief Information Officer is responsible for:
Certifying and accrediting USDA computer systems for processing collateral classified information;
Coordinating with PDSD requests for processing collateral classified information on USDA computers and establishing secure networks; and
policy_statements.target: PDSD requests for processing collateral classified information on USDA computers and establishing secure networks

policy_statements.source_text: Incorporating, where appropriate, applicable USDA information security policies and procedures into USDA policies and standards for Information Technology systems protection.
policy_statements.target: applicable USDA information security policies and procedures

policy_statements.source_text: PDSD is responsible for implementing E.O. 13526, 32 CFR Part 2001, DR 3440-001 and DM 3440-001.
This includes:
Day-to-day management of the Department’s information security program;
Issuing and/or updating Department-wide information security policies, and procedures;
policy_statements.target: Department-wide information security policies, and procedures

policy_statements.source_text: Reviewing and updating the Security Classification Guide a minimum of every five (5) years, or upon regulatory changes and incorporate original classification decisions as soon as practicable;
conditions: a minimum of every five (5) years, or upon regulatory changes

policy_statements.source_text: Coordinating the Security Classification Guide updates with users and subject matter experts;
Coordinating and providing initial security indoctrination training, annual refresher training, and security debriefings;
policy_statements.target: initial security indoctrination training, annual refresher training, and security debriefings

policy_statements.source_text: Developing and coordinating statistical data use by Agencies and Staff Offices for self-inspection report;
policy_statements.target: statistical data use by Agencies and Staff Offices for self-inspection report

policy_statements.source_text: Approving rooms for the storage, discussion, and processing of classified information up to and including Sensitive Compartmented Information;
policy_statements.target: rooms for the storage, discussion, and processing of classified information up to and including Sensitive Compartmented Information

policy_statements.source_text: Receiving reports of incidents of suspected mishandling or inadvertent disclosure of classified information and conducting requisite security inquiries when appropriate;
policy_statements.target: reports of incidents of suspected mishandling or inadvertent disclosure of classified information

policy_statements.source_text: Providing mandatory training for Original Classification Authorities each year and training every two (2) years for those personnel who create derivatively marked classified documents in accordance with §2001.71(c) and (d) of 32 CFR 2001;
policy_statements.target: mandatory training for Original Classification Authorities each year and training every two (2) years for those personnel who create derivatively marked classified documents

policy_statements.source_text: Recommending suspension of access to classified information for individuals who failed to complete mandatory training; and
policy_statements.target: suspension of access to classified information for individuals who failed to complete mandatory training

policy_statements.source_text: Providing support via training or individual support to Agencies requesting guidance on the development and marking of derivatively classified documents with respect to Part 2 of E.O 13526 and § 2001.22 of 32 CFR Part 2001.
policy_statements.target: support via training or individual support to Agencies requesting guidance on the development and marking of derivatively classified documents

policy_statements.source_text: Information Security Coordinators are responsible for being the primary liaison between their Agency and PDSD.
They are responsible for ensuring their Agency meets the requirements identified in this DR and DM 3440-001.
Information Security Coordinators shall maintain a minimum of a Secret security clearance.
policy_statements.target: a minimum of a Secret security clearance

policy_statements.source_text: Their responsibilities include:
Advising their Agency on properly marking, storing, processing, disclosing, transmitting, and destroying classified information;
Conducting self-inspections within the Agency to ensure they are properly handling classified information;
Coordinating information security refresher training;
Gathering information annually for ISOO reports;
Assisting with classification, declassification, and challenges to classification;
policy_statements.target: classification, declassification, and challenges to classification

policy_statements.source_text: Reporting security violations and concerns to PDSD; and
Maintaining a list of all individuals within their Agency with authority to apply derivative classification markings.
policy_statements.target: a list of all individuals within their Agency with authority to apply derivative classification markings

policy_statements.source_text: Employees, contractors, and individuals maintaining a security clearance for working with classified information at USDA are responsible for the following:
Adhering to the provisions of this DR and DM 3440-001;
policy_statements.actor_name: Employees, contractors, and individuals maintaining a security clearance for working with classified information at USDA
policy_statements.target: the provisions of this DR and DM 3440-001

policy_statements.source_text: Immediately reporting security irregularities and security violations to their respective information security coordinators and supervisors;
policy_statements.actor_name: Employees, contractors, and individuals maintaining a security clearance for working with classified information at USDA

policy_statements.source_text: Completing the initial security indoctrination training, annual security refresher training, security debriefings and derivative classification training as required;
policy_statements.actor_name: Employees, contractors, and individuals maintaining a security clearance for working with classified information at USDA
policy_statements.target: the initial security indoctrination training, annual security refresher training, security debriefings and derivative classification training

policy_statements.source_text: Requesting a waiver for completing mandatory training in the required time and ensuring training is completed as soon as practicable. Requests must be submitted in writing with justification for waiver; and
policy_statements.actor_name: Employees, contractors, and individuals maintaining a security clearance for working with classified information at USDA
policy_statements.target: a waiver for completing mandatory training in the required time

policy_statements.source_text: Exercising their right to challenge classified information they believe to be improperly classified and the right to appeal the agency’s decision to the ISCAP.
policy_statements.actor_name: Employees, contractors, and individuals maintaining a security clearance for working with classified information at USDA
policy_statements.target: their right to challenge classified information they believe to be improperly classified and the right to appeal the agency’s decision to the ISCAP
